data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Back
data.comment: Tooltip on the back arrow at the left end of the editor's heading bar, shown on every screen except the home screen. Pressing it returns to the screen before.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Close
data.comment: Tooltip on the close cross at the far right of the editor's heading bar, shown only on the home screen, where there is no screen to go back to. Pressing it closes the editor.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Undo
data.comment: Tooltip on the undo arrow in the editor's heading bar, shown while there is a change to undo. {action} is filled with what undoing takes back, such as "rename".

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Redo
data.comment: Tooltip on the redo arrow in the editor's heading bar, shown while there is an undone change to make again. {action} is filled with what redoing does again, such as "rename".

data.name: Sprocket.Rename.Empty
data.comment: Said under a name being typed in the editor's heading bar, when the box is empty and the thing must have a name.

data.name: Sprocket.Rename.Taken
data.comment: Said under a name being typed in the editor's heading bar, when something else already has that name.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Broken
data.value: **Something needs mending** Open it to see what.
data.comment: Tooltip on the round light at the start of a row in a list (a logic system, installation or sequence on the home screen or a logic system's screen) while the light is red because something in what the row opens needs mending.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Ran
data.comment: Tooltip on the round light at the start of a row in a list (a logic system, installation or sequence on the home screen or a logic system's screen) while the light flashes green just after the thing ran.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Idle
data.value: **Idle** Lights green when it runs, and red when something in it needs mending.
data.comment: Tooltip on the round light at the start of a row in a list (a logic system, installation or sequence on the home screen or a logic system's screen) while the light is dark: nothing ran a moment ago and nothing is broken.

data.name: Sprocket.Switch.On
data.comment: The half of an on/off switch that turns something on, on rows of the home screen and in the editor's heading bar. Short: it shares the switch with the word for off.

data.name: Sprocket.Switch.Off
data.comment: The half of an on/off switch that turns something off, on rows of the home screen and in the editor's heading bar. Short: it shares the switch with the word for on.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchOn
data.comment: Tooltip on an installation's on/off switch while the switch is off, on the installation's row on the home screen and in the heading bar of the installation panel. Shown only while the installation's logic system is switched on.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchOff
data.value: Switch this installation off and stop any running sequences.
data.comment: Tooltip on an installation's on/off switch while the switch is on, on the installation's row on the home screen and in the heading bar of the installation panel. Shown only while the installation's logic system is switched on.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchSystemOn
data.value: Switch this logic system on, locking it against changes.
data.comment: Tooltip on the on/off switch of a logic system that has no installations, while it is off: on its row on the home screen and in the editor's heading bar on its screen and its sequences' screens.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchSystemOff
data.value: Switch this logic system off, stopping its sequences and unlocking it for changes.
data.comment: Tooltip on the on/off switch of a logic system that has no installations, while it is on: on its row on the home screen and in the editor's heading bar on its screen and its sequences' screens.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchBlueprintOn
data.value: Switch on every installation of this logic system
data.comment: Tooltip on the on/off switch of a logic system that has installations, while it is off: on its row on the home screen and in the editor's heading bar on its screen and its sequences' screens. Each installation then runs where its own switch is on.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchBlueprintFirst
data.value: The logic system must be switched on first.
data.comment: Tooltip on an installation's on/off switch while its logic system is switched off and the installation's switch is dimmed and cannot be pressed: on the installation's row on the home screen and in the heading bar of the installation panel.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchBlueprintOff
data.value: Switch off every installation of this logic system
data.comment: Tooltip on the on/off switch of a logic system that has installations, while it is on: on its row on the home screen and in the editor's heading bar on its screen and its sequences' screens.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Title
data.comment: Heading of the home screen, in the editor's heading bar. {name} is filled with the grid's name, which is pressed to rename the grid, so the words either side of {name} are drawn around it, and the name is always shown exactly as it is.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.NameAbout
data.value: This grid's name. You can rename the grid here, same as in the control panel's Info tab.
data.comment: Tooltip on the grid's name in the home screen's heading, where pressing the name renames the grid.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.New
data.comment: Button on the home screen, after a plus sign meaning add, that adds a new logic system to the construct. A logic system is a set of sequences that work together, such as an airlock's.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.NewAbout
data.value: Start a new logic system on this construct.
data.comment: Tooltip on the home screen's button that adds a new logic system to the construct.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.OpenInstanceAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on an installation's row on the home screen, under its logic system; pressing the row opens that installation's installation panel. {name} is filled with the installation's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Load
data.comment: Button in the editor's heading bar on the home screen that opens the library, which holds the backups and the blueprints. Also the heading of the library screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Heading
data.comment: Heading over the list of logic systems on the home screen, shown in capitals and linked to the codex entry for logic systems.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Installations
data.comment: Heading on the home screen over a logic system's installations, under that logic system's heading row; shown in capitals and linked to the codex entry for installations.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.LoadAbout
data.value: The **library**: the logic systems on this construct, backups of constructs that lost their automation, and the blueprints in storage.
data.comment: Tooltip on the button in the editor's heading bar on the home screen that opens the library. The library holds the logic systems on this construct, backups of constructs that lost their automation, and the blueprints in storage.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Empty
data.comment: Shown on the home screen in place of the list of logic systems while the construct has none.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.MakeBlueprint
data.comment: Button on a logic system's heading row on the home screen, and in the library's details of a logic system or a backup, while the library holds no blueprint of it. Pressing it keeps a copy in the library, as a blueprint.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.MakeBlueprintAbout
data.value: Keep a copy of this logic system in the library as a **blueprint**.
data.comment: Tooltip on the button that makes a blueprint of a logic system, on its heading row on the home screen and in the library's details, shown while the library holds no blueprint of it.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.UpdateBlueprint
data.comment: Button on a logic system's heading row on the home screen, and in the library's details, once the library holds a blueprint of the logic system and the logic system was changed after it. Pressing it brings the blueprint up to date from the logic system.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.UpdateFromLibrary
data.comment: Button on a logic system's heading row on the home screen, and in the library's details of a logic system on this construct, shown where the blueprint in the library was changed after the logic system. Pressing it puts the blueprint in the logic system's place.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.UpdateFromLibraryAbout
data.value: The blueprint in the library has more recent changes. Update your construct's version.
data.comment: Tooltip on the button on a logic system's heading row on the home screen, and in the library's details, that puts the library's newer blueprint in the logic system's place; shown where the blueprint was changed after the logic system.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.UpdateBlueprintAbout
data.value: Update the blueprint from the copy on your current construct.
data.comment: Tooltip on the button on a logic system's heading row on the home screen, and in the library's details, that brings the library's blueprint up to date from the logic system; shown once the library holds a blueprint and the logic system was changed after it.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.EditBlueprint
data.comment: Tooltip on a logic system's heading row on the home screen, and on the logic system's name in the editor's heading bar on the installation panel; pressing either opens the logic system's screen. {name} is filled with the logic system's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.AddAnother
data.comment: Button on the home screen, after a plus sign meaning add, as the last line under a logic system's installations. It adds another installation: another set of blocks for the logic system, chosen on the installation panel.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.AddAnotherAbout
data.value: Install the **{name}** logic system on another set of blocks.
data.comment: Tooltip on the home screen's button under a logic system's installations that adds another installation. {name} is filled with the logic system's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Running
data.comment: Status word on the home screen, on a logic system's heading row and on an installation's row, shown while any of its sequences is running.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Numbered
data.comment: Name shown for a logic system that has no name of its own and whose blocks' names share no leading words, such as in the editor's heading bar on its screen. {number} is filled with the logic system's number.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.Numbered
data.comment: Name given to a slot Sprocket makes by itself: a slot for a set of several blocks the steps and triggers name, or the signal slot of a copied button trigger. Shown as the slot's name on a logic system's screen and the installation panel. {number} is the first number not already used, counting on from how many slots the logic system has.

data.name: Sprocket.System.InstallationPanel
data.comment: Heading on the screen of a logic system made as a blueprint, over the blueprint's description and slots: the installation panel of the installation currently shown. Shown in capitals.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.Purpose
data.comment: Heading on a slot's page, in capitals, over the box or text that says what the slot is for.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.Expects
data.comment: Heading on a slot's page, in capitals, over the one type of block the slot takes.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.AnyBlock
data.comment: On a slot's page, under the heading for the kinds of block the slot takes, when the slot takes any kind of block.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.OpenAbout
data.value: Name this slot and say what it is for.
data.comment: Tooltip on a slot's name in the slots list on a logic system's screen, while the logic system can be changed. Pressing the name opens the slot's page, where it is named and described.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.SetAsideNote
data.comment: In the picker, under a block's name in place of its kind, for a block listed first because the installation had it for a slot that was since split or merged.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.SetAside
data.comment: On the installation panel, under a slot that was split or merged and has to be filled again. {blocks} is the names of the blocks the installation had, separated by commas; the picker offers them first.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.Changed
data.comment: On the installation panel, in place of a slot's blocks, when the slot was split or merged and has to be filled again.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.MarkNew
data.comment: On a logic system's screen, under a slot's blocks, for another installation of the logic system that has not filled this new slot yet. {installation} is that installation's name; several such notes are joined by semicolons.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.MarkChanged
data.comment: On a logic system's screen, under a slot's blocks, for another installation whose blocks for the slot were set aside when the slot was split or merged. {installation} is that installation's name; several such notes are joined by semicolons.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.MarkLost
data.comment: On a logic system's screen, under a slot's blocks, for another installation that has lost one of its blocks for the slot from the construct. {installation} is that installation's name; several such notes are joined by semicolons.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.FillAgainOne
data.comment: Shown when exactly one slot of an installation was split or merged and has to be filled again: beside the Slots heading on the installation panel, and in place of the status on the installation's row on the home screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.FillAgainMany
data.comment: Shown when several slots of an installation were split or merged and have to be filled again: beside the Slots heading on the installation panel, and in place of the status on the installation's row on the home screen. {count} is how many.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Instance
data.comment: The name a new installation of a logic system is given, the first one included; {number} is the first number free, counting on from the installations there are, and is not the installation's own number. Also the name shown for an installation that has none, with {number} its place among the installations.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.InstanceOf
data.comment: An installation named in full where it is not shown under its logic system, such as in the question asked when a toolbar button chosen for a trigger already belongs to another trigger. {installation} is filled with the installation's name, {name} with the logic system's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.Keep
data.comment: Answer in the question dialog asked before deleting a blueprint from storage or forgetting a backup in the library: deletes nothing. It is the answer Enter takes.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.Confirm
data.comment: Answer in the question dialog asked before deleting a blueprint from storage or forgetting a backup in the library: deletes it.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.Final
data.comment: Warning line in the question dialog asked before deleting a blueprint from storage or forgetting a backup in the library, under the name of what is to be deleted.

data.name: Sprocket.System.NameAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on a logic system's name in the editor's heading bar on its own screen, where pressing the name renames the logic system.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Delete
data.value: Delete this logic system, and every installation of it
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin in the editor's heading bar on a logic system's screen, which deletes the logic system together with every installation of it.

data.name: Sprocket.System.DeleteInstallation
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin of an installation's row on the home screen, which deletes that installation.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Using
data.comment: Words at the top of the screen of a logic system made as a blueprint, leading a list of its installations. The installation chosen in that list is the one whose blocks fill the slots named in every sentence on the screen.

data.name: Sprocket.System.UsingAbout
data.value: Select the installation this screen works on. Its blocks fill the slots in the steps below, and blocks picked here go into its slots.
data.comment: Tooltip on the list of a logic system's installations at the top of its screen; the installation picked there fills the slots named in the screen's sentences.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Triggers
data.comment: Heading on a logic system's screen over its triggers, the things that start its sequences. Shown in capitals.

data.name: Sprocket.System.WhenAbout
data.value: Perform a task when a block sends a signal or reaches a requested state.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-trigger menu on a logic system's screen that adds a trigger started by a block's signal or state.

data.name: Sprocket.System.EveryAbout
data.value: Repeat a task at a set interval.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-trigger menu on a logic system's screen that adds a trigger started on a timer.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Trigger
data.comment: Button under the triggers on a logic system's screen, after a plus sign meaning add. It opens the add-trigger menu, offering a trigger started by something happening to a block and one started on a timer; hidden while the logic system is switched on.

data.name: Sprocket.System.TriggerAbout
data.value: Add a trigger that determines what starts a sequence.
data.comment: Tooltip on the plus button under the triggers on a logic system's screen, which opens the menu of triggers to add.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Sequences
data.comment: Heading on a logic system's screen over its sequences, the named runs of steps its triggers start. Shown in capitals.

data.name: Sprocket.System.NewSequence
data.comment: Button under the sequences on a logic system's screen, after a plus sign meaning add, that adds a sequence with nothing to start it yet; hidden while the logic system is switched on.

data.name: Sprocket.System.NewSequenceAbout
data.value: Add a sequence that can run several steps in order.
data.comment: Tooltip on the plus button under the sequences on a logic system's screen, which adds a new sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.System.NoSequences
data.comment: Shown on a logic system's screen in place of the list of sequences while the logic system has none.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Copy
data.value: Copy this sequence. The copy starts switched off and without triggers.
data.comment: Tooltip on the copy mark of a sequence's row on a logic system's screen, for a sequence that a trigger starts.

data.name: Sprocket.System.CopyUnstarted
data.value: Copy this sequence. The copy starts switched off.
data.comment: Tooltip on the copy mark of a sequence's row on a logic system's screen, for a sequence that no trigger starts.

data.name: Sprocket.System.OpenSequence
data.value: Open **{name}** to see and change its steps.
data.comment: Tooltip on a sequence's row on a logic system's screen; pressing the row opens the sequence's screen. {name} is filled with the sequence's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.Live
data.comment: Badge on a trigger's row on a logic system's screen, shown while what the trigger watches for is true at this instant, such as a door standing open.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.Delete
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin at the end of a trigger's row on a logic system's screen, while the trigger can be deleted.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.Copy
data.comment: Tooltip on the copy mark near the end of a trigger's row on a logic system's screen, while the trigger can be copied.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.CopiedButton
data.value: Each button starts one trigger, so select a new button for this copy.
data.comment: Note under a trigger's row on a logic system's screen, for a copy of a button trigger, until a button is first picked for the copy. Its button part stays empty until then.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.BlocksAbout
data.value: Select the block that fires this trigger.
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of a trigger's sentence, on a logic system's screen, that names the block that starts it. Pressing the part changes the block.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.WhatAbout
data.value: Select what the block must do to fire this trigger.
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of a trigger's sentence, on a logic system's screen, that names what happens to the block to start it. Pressing the part changes it.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.DoesAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of a trigger's sentence, on a logic system's screen, that names the sequence it starts or the action it does. Pressing the part changes it.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.RateAbout
data.value: Change how often it should run.
data.comment: Tooltip on the length in an Every trigger's sentence on a logic system's screen, which says how often the trigger runs. Pressing it opens the length panel.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.TargetsAbout
data.value: Select which blocks this trigger acts on.
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of a trigger's sentence, on a logic system's screen, that names the blocks the trigger's own action acts on. Pressing the part changes them.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.NameAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on a sequence's name in the editor's heading bar on its own screen, where pressing the name renames the sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DoSomething
data.comment: Choice in the add-step menu on a sequence's screen, which opens from the plus button at the end of the sequence or of a branch of an if; it adds a task, a step acting on blocks, and asks which blocks and what to do before it adds.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DoSomethingAbout
data.value: Perform an action on blocks or set one of their values.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-step menu on a sequence's screen that adds a task: an action on blocks, or setting one of their values.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Step
data.comment: Button on a sequence's screen, after a plus sign meaning add, at the end of the sequence and at the end of each branch of an if. It opens the add-step menu of the kinds of step: task, wait, run, stop and if.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.StepAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on the plus button on a sequence's screen, at the end of the sequence or of a branch of an if, that opens the menu of steps to add.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.WaitAbout
data.value: Wait a set time before the next step.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-step menu on a sequence's screen that adds a wait of a set time.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Held
data.comment: Line shown while another player is editing, in place of the buttons that add things on a logic system's screen, a sequence's screen and a blueprint slot's screen; also the tooltip on parts that cannot be pressed meanwhile. {holder} is filled with that player's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Delete
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin of a sequence's row on a logic system's screen, and on the bin in the editor's heading bar on a sequence's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DeleteStep
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin at the end of a step's row on a sequence's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.CopyStep
data.comment: Tooltip on the copy mark of a step's row on a sequence's screen. An if is copied with the steps in it.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.ActionAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on the action named in a step's sentence on a sequence's screen; pressing it opens the picker to choose what the step does.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.BlocksAbout
data.value: Select which blocks this step acts on.
data.comment: Tooltip on the blocks named in a step's sentence on a sequence's screen; pressing them opens the picker to choose which blocks the step acts on.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.OptionsAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on the options of an action, such as a piston's position and speed, in a step's sentence on a sequence's screen and in a trigger's sentence on a logic system's screen; pressing them opens the picker on the action's options.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.NewValueAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on the new value in the sentence of a step or trigger that sets a value of blocks, on a sequence's screen and on a logic system's screen; pressing it opens the picker on that value.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.ComparedAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on the comparison in an if's sentence on a sequence's screen, such as "is" or "is below"; pressing it opens a menu of the comparisons the value can be checked with.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.ReadAbout
data.value: Choose how the blocks are read.
data.comment: Tooltip on how an if reads its blocks in its sentence on a sequence's screen, where it names several: "any", "all", "the sum of" or "the average of"; pressing it opens a menu of those.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.CheckedAbout
data.value: Change the value to check for.
data.comment: Tooltip on the value an if checks blocks for, in the if's sentence on a sequence's screen; pressing it opens the picker on that value.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.LengthAbout
data.value: Change how long it should wait.
data.comment: Tooltip on a wait step's length in its sentence on a sequence's screen; pressing it opens the panel where the length is given.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DragStep
data.comment: Tooltip on the drag handle of a step's row on a sequence's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.PauseStep
data.value: Pause this step. The sequence skips it until it is resumed.
data.comment: Tooltip on the pause mark of a step's row on a sequence's screen, while the step is not paused; pressing it pauses the step.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.UnpauseStep
data.value: Paused: the sequence skips this step. Press to resume it.
data.comment: Tooltip on the pause mark of a step's row on a sequence's screen, lit while the step is paused; pressing it resumes the step.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SkippedBusyOne
data.comment: Shown in the line saying what a sequence is doing, on the sequence's screen, when the sequence was started once while it was already running and so did not run that time.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SkippedBusy
data.comment: Shown in the line saying what a sequence is doing, on the sequence's screen, when the sequence was started while it was already running and so did not run. {busy} is filled with how many times, always more than one.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SkippedOffOne
data.comment: Shown in the line saying what a sequence is doing, on the sequence's screen, when the sequence was started once while it was switched off and so did not run that time.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SkippedOff
data.comment: Shown in the line saying what a sequence is doing, on the sequence's screen, when the sequence was started while it was switched off and so did not run. {off} is filled with how many times, always more than one.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SkippedBothOne
data.value: 1 start missed while running, {off} refused while switched off
data.comment: Shown in the line saying what a sequence is doing, on the sequence's screen, when the sequence was started once while already running and also while switched off, and so did not run those times. {off} is filled with how many times it was started while switched off.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SkippedBoth
data.value: {busy} starts missed while running, {off} refused while switched off
data.comment: Shown in the line saying what a sequence is doing, on the sequence's screen, when the sequence was started both while already running and while switched off, and so did not run. {busy} is filled with how many times it was started while running, always more than one, {off} with how many times while switched off.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.WaitTypedAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on the number box where a length of time is typed: in the panel for a wait's length on a sequence's screen, the panel for a timer trigger's interval on a logic system's screen, and the column choosing how often a new timer trigger fires.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Different
data.value: This block holds a program from a different version.
data.comment: Banner at the top of every screen of the editor when the block holds a program written by a version of the mod that cannot read it.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.DifferentDetail
data.value: This version cannot read it, so this screen starts empty. The block keeps the old program until you change something here. Then it is gone for good.
data.comment: Shown when the banner saying the block holds a program from a different version is opened.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Broken
data.value: This block holds a program with an error in it.
data.comment: Banner at the top of every screen of the editor when the block's program has an error in its text, so none of it was loaded.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.BrokenDetail
data.value: None of it runs, and this screen starts empty. Edit the text to mend it. The block keeps the old program until you change something here. Then it is gone for good.
data.comment: Shown when the banner saying the block's program has an error in it is opened.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Mend
data.comment: Button on the banner saying the block's program has an error in it: opens the program's text, where the error can be mended.

data.name: Sprocket.Script.Title
data.comment: The heading of the script page in developer mode, which shows the program as text to edit by hand, and the entry along the bottom of the editor that opens that page, shown only in developer mode.

data.name: Sprocket.Script.Apply
data.comment: The button on the script page in developer mode that reads the text in the page's box and, where it has no error, puts it in place of the program.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Trouble
data.comment: Shown in an opened banner about a program that could not be read, under its explanation. {trouble} is what went wrong, in the program reader's own words, which are not translated.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Replace
data.comment: Button on the banner saying the block holds a program from a different version, and the answer in the question dialog asked before that program is replaced: replaces it.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Question
data.value: Replace the program this block holds? The one that could not be read will be gone.
data.comment: Question dialog asked before the first change that replaces a program that could not be read, and when the Replace button on the banner about it is pressed.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Keep
data.comment: Answer in the question dialog asked before replacing a program that could not be read: changes nothing. It is the answer Enter takes.

data.name: Sprocket.Lease.Holder
data.comment: Banner at the top of every screen of the editor while another player is editing the same block's automation, so this editor only shows it. {holder} is that player's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Lease.Detail
data.value: Only one person can edit at a time. Reopen this once they're done to make changes.
data.comment: Shown when the banner saying another player is editing this block's automation is opened.

data.name: Sprocket.Button.Starts
data.comment: Question shown under the picked button after a button is picked for a button trigger or a signal slot, when another trigger already uses it to start a sequence. {block} is the button panel's name, {sequence} the sequence's name, and {blockset} the logic system's name or the installation's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Button.Stops
data.comment: Question shown under the picked button after a button is picked for a button trigger or a signal slot, when another trigger already uses it to stop a sequence. {block} is the button panel's name, {sequence} the sequence's name, and {blockset} the logic system's name or the installation's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Button.Acts
data.comment: Question shown under the picked button after a button is picked for a button trigger or a signal slot, when another trigger already uses it to act on blocks directly rather than start a sequence. {block} is the button panel's name and {blockset} the logic system's name or the installation's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Button.Elsewhere
data.value: Button {button} of **{block}** already does something else.
data.comment: Question shown under the picked button after a button is picked for a button trigger or a signal slot, when the button's toolbar slot holds something no Sprocket trigger put there, such as the game's own action or another block's automation. {block} is the button panel's name and {button} the button's number, counting from 1.

data.name: Sprocket.Button.TakeOver
data.comment: Answer to the question asked when a picked button is already in use: gives the button to the trigger or slot being made, taking it from whatever had it.

data.name: Sprocket.Button.LeaveAlone
data.comment: Answer that changes nothing, in several question dialogs: when a picked button is already in use, when deleting an if or a branch of one on a sequence's screen, and before removing every logic system from the Paused screen. It is the answer Enter takes.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Search
data.comment: Hint in a search box that narrows a list by typing: in the picker's columns, in the picker's list of kinds of block, and in the library.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Done
data.comment: Button at the right end of the editor's heading bar that finishes the screen, on a logic system's screen, a sequence's screen, the installation panel, a blueprint slot's screen and the picker. Also the button that closes the panel where a wait's length or a timer trigger's interval is given, keeping the length in it.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.DoneAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on the Done button in the editor's heading bar on a logic system's screen, a sequence's screen, the installation panel and a blueprint slot's screen, where every change is kept as soon as it is made.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.DoneFirst
data.value: Select something in every column first.
data.comment: Tooltip on the Done button in the editor's heading bar in the picker, and on the page choosing how often a timer trigger fires, while it cannot be pressed yet.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.DoneAbout
data.value: Use what is selected and return.
data.comment: Tooltip on the Done button in the editor's heading bar in the picker, and on the page choosing how often a timer trigger fires, once it can be pressed; pressing it uses what is chosen and goes back.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Back
data.comment: Tooltip on the narrow folded column at the left edge of the picker, which turns back to the picker's page before.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Next
data.comment: Tooltip on the narrow folded column at the right edge of the picker, which turns on to the picker's page after.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.ClearTyped
data.comment: Tooltip on the cross at the end of a search box in the picker, which empties the box.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.EveryKind
data.comment: Tooltip on the cross beside the kind of block that the picker's column of blocks is narrowed to; pressing it shows every kind again.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.ShowHidden
data.comment: Tooltip on the closed eye at the end of the heading of the picker's column of blocks; pressing it also lists the blocks set not to show in the toolbar config.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.HideHidden
data.comment: Tooltip on the open eye at the end of the heading of the picker's column of blocks; pressing it takes the blocks set not to show in the toolbar config out of the list again.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.AllShown
data.comment: Line in the picker's column of blocks, over the list, while it shows every block. {count} is filled with how many blocks there are.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SomeShown
data.comment: Line in the picker's column of blocks, over the list, while a search or a kind narrows it to some blocks. {shown} is filled with how many are shown, {count} with how many there are.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Anything
data.comment: Entry at the top of the list of kinds of block in the picker's column of blocks, which narrows to no kind at all; also the word on the line that opens that list while no kind is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.KindAbout
data.value: Show only one kind of block.
data.comment: Tooltip on the line in the picker's column of blocks that opens the list of kinds of block.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.KeepQuestion
data.comment: Question dialog asked on leaving the picker by going back after changing what it opened on, and on leaving the page where a screen's text or a block's Custom Data is written by going back after changing the text.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.KeepThem
data.comment: Answer in the question dialog asked on leaving the picker, or the page a screen's text or a block's Custom Data is written on, after changing what it opened on; it keeps the changes and finishes, and is the answer the Enter key gives.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.DiscardThem
data.comment: Answer in the question dialog asked on leaving the picker, or the page a screen's text or a block's Custom Data is written on, after changing what it opened on; it leaves without keeping the changes.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Blocks
data.comment: Heading of the picker's column of blocks, shown in capitals.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NoBlocksHappen
data.value: No block on this construct has a signal or state that can start a trigger.
data.comment: Shown in the picker's column of blocks, in place of the list, when nothing on the construct has anything that can happen to it; seen while picking what starts a trigger.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.WhatToCheck
data.comment: Heading of the picker's column listing what an if can check of the chosen blocks, shown in capitals.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NothingChecked
data.value: The selected blocks have nothing in common that can be checked.
data.comment: Shown in the picker's column of what an if can check, in place of the list, when the chosen blocks have nothing in common that can be checked.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NoBlocksChecked
data.value: No block on this construct has a value or state to check.
data.comment: Shown in the picker's column of blocks, in place of the list, when nothing on the construct has anything that can be checked; seen while picking what an if checks.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NoBlocksDone
data.value: No block on this construct has an action or a value to set.
data.comment: Shown in the picker's column of blocks, in place of the list, when nothing on the construct has anything that can be done to it; seen while picking what a step or a trigger's own task does.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.WhatHappens
data.comment: Heading of the picker's column listing what can happen to the chosen blocks, seen while picking what starts a trigger; shown in capitals.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.WhatToDo
data.comment: Heading of the picker's column of what can be done to the chosen blocks, seen while picking what a step or a trigger's own task does; shown in capitals.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NothingHappens
data.value: Those blocks have nothing in common that can happen to them.
data.comment: Shown in the picker's column of what can happen to the chosen blocks, in place of the list, when the chosen blocks have nothing in common that can happen to them.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NothingDone
data.value: Those blocks have nothing in common that can be done to them.
data.comment: Shown in the picker's column of what can be done to the chosen blocks, in place of the list, when the chosen blocks have nothing in common that can be done to them.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.WhatItDoes
data.comment: Heading of the picker's column choosing what a trigger does, beside what starts it, in the picker and on the page choosing how often a timer trigger fires; shown in capitals.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NonePicked
data.comment: Line under the heading of the picker's column of blocks while no block is picked.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.OnePicked
data.comment: Line under the heading of the picker's column of blocks while one block is picked.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SomePicked
data.comment: Line under the heading of the picker's column of blocks while several blocks are picked. {count} is filled with how many.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.AverageNote
data.comment: Banner at the top of the picker's column of what an if can check, shown while "the average of" is chosen in the column of blocks, saying why nothing but numbers is listed.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SumNote
data.comment: Banner at the top of the picker's column of what an if can check, shown while "the sum of" is chosen in the column of blocks, saying why nothing but numbers is listed.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Status
data.comment: The first group heading in the picker's column of what an if can check, in the organized view: over the values that are each a block's status, such as a door's status or whether it is working, which a check reads as the block itself ("if Airlock Door is open").

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Values
data.comment: Group heading in the picker's column of what can be done to the chosen blocks while it lists them the way the game's terminal does, over a block's values.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.ToolbarActions
data.comment: Group heading in the picker's column of what can be done to the chosen blocks while it lists them the way the game's terminal does, over a block's toolbar actions.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.ToOrganized
data.comment: Link at the end of the heading of the picker's column of what can be done to the chosen blocks, shown while the column lists them the way the game's terminal does; pressing it goes back to the organized list. An angle mark is drawn before it, pointing the way the link goes.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.ToTerminal
data.comment: Link at the end of the heading of the picker's column of what can be done to the chosen blocks, shown while the column shows the organized list; pressing it lists everything the blocks offer in the game's terminal, under the game's own names. An angle mark is drawn after it, pointing the way the link goes.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.TerminalNote
data.value: Everything these blocks offer in the terminal, under the terminal's own names. Using them is your own call. The organized list holds the ones known to work with the automation.
data.comment: Banner at the top of the picker's column of what can be done to the chosen blocks, shown for as long as the column lists them the way the game's terminal does.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Shared
data.value: Showing only what the picked blocks share
data.comment: Note at the top of the picker's column of what can be done to the chosen blocks when several blocks are picked and the list is narrowed to what they all share.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Planned
data.comment: Note at the top of the picker's column of what can be done to the chosen blocks, in the organized list, naming what the picked blocks are to offer that is not built yet. {planned} is filled with a comma-separated list, such as "moving items".

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NoteAndShared
data.comment: Note at the top of the picker's column of what can be done to the chosen blocks when two notes apply at once. {note} is filled with either the terminal list's banner or the note naming what is not built yet, and {shared} with the note saying the list shows only what the picked blocks share.

data.name: Sprocket.Plan.MovingItems
data.comment: One item in the picker's "Still to come" note over what the chosen blocks offer, naming something not built yet for blocks with an inventory.

data.name: Sprocket.Plan.SorterList
data.comment: One item in the picker's "Still to come" note over what the chosen blocks offer, naming something not built yet for a conveyor sorter.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Waits
data.value: This takes time to finish. The sequence can wait for it, or go straight on while it runs.
data.comment: Tooltip on an action marked with the clock, one that takes time to finish: on its row in the picker and on its part of a sentence. Also the tooltip on a step's sentence on a sequence's screen when the step starts such an action and goes straight on.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.RunAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice at the top of the picker's column choosing what a trigger does that makes the trigger start the sequence chosen in that column.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.StopAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice at the top of the picker's column choosing what a trigger does that makes the trigger stop the sequence chosen in that column.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SingleAction
data.comment: Choice in the picker's column choosing what a trigger does: the trigger does one task on some blocks, chosen on the picker's page after; the trailing ellipsis says a page follows. Offered only in developer mode, or where the trigger already does a task of its own.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SingleActionAbout
data.value: Perform a single task on some blocks.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the picker's column choosing what a trigger does that makes the trigger do a single task of its own on some blocks, without a sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SingleTask
data.comment: Title in the editor's heading bar of the picker page choosing a trigger's own task, shown until something is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NewSequence
data.comment: Choice in the picker's column choosing what a trigger does: the trigger starts a new sequence made for it. Shown while the trigger starts a sequence rather than stopping one.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NewSequenceAbout
data.value: Make a new sequence for this trigger to start.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the picker's column choosing what a trigger does that makes a new sequence for the trigger to start.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Sequences
data.comment: Heading in the picker's column choosing what a trigger does, over the logic system's existing sequences the trigger may start, shown while the trigger starts a sequence rather than stopping one.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.HowOftenQuestion
data.comment: Title in the editor's heading bar of the page choosing how often a timer trigger fires.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.HowOften
data.comment: Heading of the column where a timer trigger's interval is given, on the page choosing how often it fires; shown in capitals.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.NameAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on the installation's name in the editor's heading bar on the installation panel. Pressing the name renames the installation.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Parts
data.comment: Heading over the list of slots: in capitals on a logic system's screen and on the installation panel, where each slot is filled with blocks, and in the library over the names of a logic system's required slots.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.StillOne
data.comment: On the installation panel, beside the Slots heading, when exactly one slot that needs a block has none.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.StillMany
data.comment: On the installation panel, beside the Slots heading, when several slots that need a block have none. {count} is how many, always more than one.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.FromLead
data.comment: In the editor's heading bar on the installation panel, between the installation's name and the name of its logic system, which can be pressed to open the logic system's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.FromAfter
data.comment: In the editor's heading bar on the installation panel, right after the name of the installation's logic system. Empty in English; for languages that need a word after the name.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Gone
data.comment: On the installation panel, on a slot whose block is no longer on the construct and that has no other block. {name} is what the lost block was called.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Description
data.comment: Heading on a logic system's screen, in capitals, over the box its description is written in. Shown only while the logic system can be changed.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.DescriptionHint
data.value: What this logic system does, and what whoever fills it in needs to know.
data.comment: Placeholder in the empty description box on a logic system's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.AboutHint
data.comment: Placeholder in the empty box on a slot's page where what the slot is for is written.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.NameBoxAbout
data.value: The slot's name, as everyone filling in this logic system sees it.
data.comment: Tooltip on the slot's name in the editor's heading bar on a slot's page. Pressing the name renames the slot.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.RequiredAbout
data.value: Set whether an installation of this logic system may leave this slot empty.
data.comment: Tooltip on the required/optional switch on a slot's page.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.Preview
data.comment: A button by the description box on a logic system's screen and on a slot's screen: shows the text as it will read in place of the box it is written in.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.Edit
data.comment: A button by the description box on a logic system's screen and on a slot's screen, while the text is shown as it reads: goes back to the box it is written in.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.Open
data.comment: Button at the right end of a step's field for text written over several lines, such as a screen's text or a block's Custom Data, which shows only the start of it: opens a page of its own to write the whole text on.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.OpenAbout
data.value: Write the whole text on a page of its own.
data.comment: Tooltip on the Edit button at the right end of a step's field for text written over several lines.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.Count
data.comment: Above the box on the page where a screen's text or a block's Custom Data is written. {count} is how many characters the text has now, a line break counting as one; {most} is how many the block holds, the most it can be.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.Markup
data.comment: A button by the description box on a logic system's screen and on a slot's screen: opens the codex's guide to the marks rich text can be written with.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.MarkupAbout
data.value: Show the guide to formatting text.
data.comment: The tooltip on the button by the description box on a logic system's screen and on a slot's screen that opens the codex's guide to formatting text.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.PreviewAbout
data.value: Show the text as others will see it.
data.comment: The tooltip on the button by the description box on a logic system's screen and on a slot's screen that shows the text as it will read.

data.name: Sprocket.Color.Hue
data.comment: Tooltip on the H slider of the color picker in the picker's values column.

data.name: Sprocket.Color.Saturation
data.comment: Tooltip on the S slider of the color picker in the picker's values column.

data.name: Sprocket.Color.Brightness
data.comment: Tooltip on the V slider of the color picker in the picker's values column.

data.name: Sprocket.Color.CodeAbout
data.value: Enter a color as #RRGGBB, or #RRGGBBAA to include its opacity.
data.comment: Tooltip on the box under the sliders of the color picker, in the picker's values column, where a color code is typed.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Required
data.comment: On a slot's page, the half of the required/optional switch for a slot that must be filled with a block. Short: it shares the switch with the word for optional.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Optional
data.comment: On a slot's page, the half of the required/optional switch for a slot that may be left without a block. Short: it shares the switch with the word for required.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.OpenSequence
data.comment: Button on the installation panel beside what is wrong with the installation, opening the sequence at fault as that installation runs it. {name} is the sequence's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.NoneFits
data.value: No block on this construct can fill this slot.
data.comment: In the picker, in the empty block list, when a slot is being filled and no block on the construct can fill it.

data.name: Sprocket.System.TurnOffToEdit
data.value: The system must be turned off in order to make changes safely.
data.comment: Tooltip on a part or button that cannot be pressed while its logic system is switched on: the copy marks and bins of trigger and sequence rows and the slot rows on a logic system's screen, and the parts of steps on a sequence's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Locked
data.value: {name} must be turned off in order to be edited safely.
data.comment: Line shown while a logic system is switched on, in place of the buttons that change it, on the logic system's screen, a sequence's screen and a blueprint slot's screen; also the tooltip on the dimmed bin in the editor's heading bar on a sequence's screen. {name} is filled with the logic system's name, except on the installation panel, where the line shows while the installation is on and {name} is the installation's name.

data.name: Sprocket.System.SwitchOnQuestion
data.comment: Question dialog asked on leaving a logic system's screen when the logic system was changed and is still switched off. {name} is filled with the logic system's name.

data.name: Sprocket.System.SwitchItOn
data.comment: Answer in the question dialog asked on leaving a changed logic system that is still switched off; it switches the logic system on.

data.name: Sprocket.System.LeaveItOff
data.comment: Answer in the question dialog asked on leaving a changed logic system that is still switched off; it leaves the logic system switched off, and is the answer the Enter key gives.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.SwitchOffQuestion
data.comment: First line of a question dialog asked when the switch of a logic system that has installations is turned off. {name} is the logic system's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.SwitchOffStops
data.value: This stops every installation of it on this construct:
data.comment: In the question dialog asked before switching off a logic system that has installations, over a bulleted list of those installations.

data.name: Sprocket.Dialog.More
data.comment: Last line of a bulleted list in a question dialog, standing for the names too many to show, such as in the question asked before switching off a logic system with many installations. {count} is how many are not shown, always more than one.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.KeepRunning
data.comment: Answer in the question dialog asked before switching off a logic system that has installations: leaves the logic system switched on. It is the answer Enter takes.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.SwitchThemOff
data.comment: Answer in the question dialog asked before switching off a logic system that has installations: switches the logic system off.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.SwitchOffRunning
data.value: Anything running now stops where it is.
data.comment: Last line of the question dialog asked before switching off a logic system that has installations, shown while any of its installations is running.

data.name: Sprocket.Prompt.Continue
data.comment: Not used on any screen. Meant as a button beside a box a name is typed into, that gives the name.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Off
data.comment: A sequence's state, shown on its row on a logic system's screen and in the line saying what it is doing on its own screen, while its logic system is switched off.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Running
data.comment: A sequence's state, shown on its row on a logic system's screen and in the line saying what it is doing on its own screen, while it is running.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.RunningWaiting
data.comment: A sequence's state, shown on its row on a logic system's screen and in the line saying what it is doing on its own screen, while it is running and held at a step it is waiting for.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Ready
data.comment: A sequence's state, shown on its row on a logic system's screen and in the line saying what it is doing on its own screen, while it is not running and is ready to be started.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Stopped
data.comment: A sequence's state, shown on its row on a logic system's screen when its last run was stopped from outside before it finished; said until it runs again. On the sequence's own screen a longer line naming the step and what stopped it is shown instead.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.StoppedBySequence
data.comment: A sequence's state, shown in the line saying what it is doing on its own screen, when another sequence stopped its last run before it finished; said until it runs again. {step} is filled with the number of the step it was at, {sequence} with the name of the sequence that stopped it.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.StoppedByTrigger
data.value: stopped at step {step} by a trigger
data.comment: A sequence's state, shown in the line saying what it is doing on its own screen, when a trigger stopped its last run before it finished; said until it runs again. {step} is filled with the number of the step it was at.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.StoppedBySwitch
data.value: stopped at step {step} when switched off
data.comment: A sequence's state, shown in the line saying what it is doing on its own screen, when its logic system, or the installation it ran on, was switched off during its last run; said once it is switched on again, until it runs again. {step} is filled with the number of the step it was at.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.StoppedByHand
data.comment: A sequence's state, shown in the line saying what it is doing on its own screen, when somebody stopped its last run from the editor before it finished; said until it runs again. {step} is filled with the number of the step it was at.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.RunNow
data.comment: Tooltip on the play button in the editor's heading bar on a sequence's screen, and on the play button of each sequence's row on a logic system's screen, while the sequence is not running; pressing it runs the sequence by hand.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.StopNow
data.value: Stop this sequence where it is
data.comment: Tooltip on the stop button in the editor's heading bar on a sequence's screen, and on the stop button of each sequence's row on a logic system's screen, while the sequence is running; pressing it stops the sequence and leaves every block as it is.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Numbered
data.comment: Name of a sequence nobody has named, shown on its row on a logic system's screen and in the editor's heading bar on its own screen; also the name a new sequence is given. {number} is filled with the sequence's number.

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.EmptySlot
data.value: The {slot} slot is empty. Fill it on the installation panel.
data.comment: Problem when a slot of a blueprint that a step or trigger needs has no block in this installation; {slot} is the slot's name as the blueprint's author gave it. Shown under the step's line on a sequence's screen (on the bar at the top for a trigger's slot), on the sequence's or trigger's row on a logic system's screen, and under the logic system's row on the home screen and at the top of the installation panel.

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.BlockOff
data.value: {block} is switched off. Switch it on first.
data.comment: Problem when a step asked a switched-off block for something it waits for, so the run ended there; {block} is the block's name. Shown under the step's line on a sequence's screen and on the sequence's row on a logic system's screen; on the home screen (under the logic system's row) and at the top of the installation panel it follows the step number, as in "Step 3: ...".

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.BlockStalled
data.comment: Problem while a step waits on a block that is switched off, unpowered or broken, so the run holds; {block} is the block's name. Shown under the step's line on a sequence's screen and on the sequence's row on a logic system's screen; on the home screen (under the logic system's row) and at the top of the installation panel it follows the step number, as in "Step 3: ...".

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.BlockTrouble
data.comment: What a block says is wrong, as a sentence naming it, such as "Airlock Vent cannot fill because the room is not airtight."; {block} is the block's name and {trouble} the block's own words for what is wrong, a phrase beginning with a verb, such as "cannot fill because the room is not airtight". Shown under the step's line on a sequence's screen, on the sequence's row on a logic system's screen, and after the step number on the home screen and the installation panel, as in "Step 3: ..." or "Stopped at step 3: ...".

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.AtStep
data.comment: The line under a logic system's row on the home screen, and at the top of the installation panel, saying what is wrong at a step of a sequence that has not been given a name; {step} is the step's number on the sequence's screen and {problem} is the sentence saying what is wrong.

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.AtNamedStep
data.comment: The line under a logic system's row on the home screen, and at the top of the installation panel, saying what is wrong at a step of a named sequence; {sequence} is the sequence's name, {step} the step's number on its screen and {problem} the sentence saying what is wrong.

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.InSequence
data.comment: The line under a logic system's row on the home screen, and at the top of the installation panel, saying what is wrong with a named sequence at no one step, such as with what starts it; {sequence} is the sequence's name and {problem} the sentence saying what is wrong.

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.NoBlock
data.value: This trigger is missing its block.
data.comment: Problem on a trigger that has no block chosen to start it. Shown on the trigger's row on a logic system's screen and on the bar at the top of the sequence's screen, and under the logic system's row on the home screen and at the top of the installation panel.

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.NoMoment

data.comment: Problem on a trigger whose block has nothing chosen for what must happen to it to start the sequence, used where the block's name is not known. Shown on the trigger's row on a logic system's screen and on the bar at the top of the sequence's screen, and under the logic system's row on the home screen and at the top of the installation panel.

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.NoMomentOf

data.comment: Problem on a trigger whose block has nothing chosen for what must happen to it to start the sequence; {block} is the block's name. data.name: Sprocket.Problem.NeverTriggered
data.value: This trigger can't fire, for an unknown reason.
data.comment: Problem on a button trigger that cannot fire where the cause was not found and no block can be named for it: the fallback beside the known causes (the button changed, not set up yet, no block, nothing selected). Shown on the trigger's row on a logic system's screen and on the bar at the top of the sequence's screen, and under the logic system's row on the home screen and at the top of the installation panel.

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.ButtonChanged
data.value: {block}'s button was changed in its toolbar.
data.comment: Problem on a button trigger whose toolbar slot was emptied or given something else in the game; {block} is the name of the block whose toolbar holds the button. Shown on the trigger's row on a logic system's screen and on the bar at the top of the sequence's screen, and under the logic system's row on the home screen and at the top of the installation panel.

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.Unset
data.value: {block}'s button isn't set up for this trigger yet.

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.MissingSource

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.MissingTarget

data.comment: In the admin settings, the tooltip on the first choice in each setting's list on the tab for this world, the choice that follows the value set on the tab for every world. Every world in the text is that tab's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Admin.DefaultEveryTick
data.comment: In the admin settings, on the tab for this world, the first choice in the list of the setting that caps how often timers and block checks repeat: it follows the value on the tab for every world, which is every tick.

data.name: Sprocket.Admin.DefaultEveryTen
data.comment: In the admin settings, on the tab for this world, the first choice in the list of the setting that caps how often timers and block checks repeat: it follows the value on the tab for every world, which is every 10 ticks.

data.name: Sprocket.Admin.DefaultEveryHundred
data.comment: In the admin settings, on the tab for this world, the first choice in the list of the setting that caps how often timers and block checks repeat: it follows the value on the tab for every world, which is every 100 ticks.

data.name: Sprocket.Admin.DefaultOn
data.comment: In the admin settings, on the tab for this world, the first choice in the list of the developer mode setting: it follows the value on the tab for every world, which has developer mode on.

data.name: Sprocket.Admin.DefaultOff
data.comment: In the admin settings, on the tab for this world, the first choice in the list of the developer mode setting: it follows the value on the tab for every world, which has developer mode off.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.WaitsHere
data.value: Steps below wait until this one, and any still running above it, are done. Press to let them run alongside.
data.comment: Tooltip on the clock and words under a step that takes time, on a sequence's screen, while the sequence waits there for the step to finish; pressing them makes the sequence go straight on. Shown when the world's admin settings show waits in sequences as a switch on each step.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.CarriesOn
data.value: Steps below run alongside this one. Press to make them wait until it's done.
data.comment: Tooltip on the clock and words under a step that takes time, on a sequence's screen, while the sequence goes straight on from the step; pressing them makes the sequence wait there. Shown when the world's admin settings show waits in sequences as a switch on each step.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.AwaitAbout
data.value: Wait until every ![](mark:awaited) task started above has finished.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-step menu on a sequence's screen that adds a row waiting for every task started before it, offered when the world's admin settings show waits as steps of their own. ![](mark:awaited) draws the mark a task waited for carries.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.AwaitRow
data.value: The ![](mark:awaited) tasks started above, back to the last await, run together. The sequence waits here until every task has finished.
data.comment: Tooltip on the words of a row waiting for every task started before it, on a sequence's screen, when the world's admin settings show waits as steps of their own. The row reads "await all pending tasks", which stays English; ![](mark:awaited) draws the mark a task waited for carries.

data.name: Sprocket.Change.WaitHere
data.comment: On the tooltips of the undo and redo arrows in the editor's heading bar, after the word Undo or Redo, on a logic system's screen and the screens opened from it (its sequences' screens, its installation panel and its slots' screens). Shows when the change to be undone or redone is setting a step on a sequence's screen so the sequence waits for it to finish before going on.

data.name: Sprocket.Change.CarryOn
data.comment: On the tooltips of the undo and redo arrows in the editor's heading bar, after the word Undo or Redo, on a logic system's screen and the screens opened from it (its sequences' screens, its installation panel and its slots' screens). Shows when the change to be undone or redone is setting a step on a sequence's screen so the sequence goes straight on without waiting for it to finish.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.WaitForCompletion
data.comment: Words beside a clock under a step that takes time, on a sequence's screen, while the sequence waits for the step to finish; pressing them makes the sequence go straight on. Shown when the world's admin settings show waits in sequences as a switch on each step.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DoNotWait
data.comment: Words beside a clock under a step that takes time, on a sequence's screen, while the sequence goes straight on from the step; pressing them makes the sequence wait for it. Shown when the world's admin settings show waits in sequences as a switch on each step.

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.NothingToAwait
data.value: This await has nothing to wait for, because no step above it takes time.
data.comment: Warning on an await (a wait for what is running) when no step since the previous await takes time to finish. Shown under the await's line on a sequence's screen and on the sequence's row on a logic system's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Admin.Spine
data.comment: In the admin settings, the label of a trial's checkbox that draws a pulsing line joining the lines on a sequence's screen lit up by the wait or step under the pointer.

data.name: Sprocket.Admin.SpineAbout
data.value: A pulsing line beside the line numbers joins the lines that light up when the pointer rests on a wait or a step, and runs on to lines scrolled out of view.
data.comment: In the admin settings, the line under the checkbox of the trial that draws a pulsing line joining the lines lit up on a sequence's screen.
